title:
New launch or nearly new?
*Check the gap*

lines.say: You're choosing between a new launch and a nearly new condo next door. Check the gap first.
Say the new launch is 2,400 dollars per square foot, and the five year old condo is 1,800.
A big gap like that often pulls the older one up over time, as buyers priced out of the new project look next door.
lines.cap: a big gap often *pulls it up*

lines.say: But if the gap is small, say 2,400 against 2,250, the newer one usually gives more for your money.
lines.cap: small gap? the *newer one* often wins

lines.say: Same street, different answer. It depends on the gap.
Most people decide this wrongly. Comment why to see the mistake.

caption:
New launch or nearly new condo next door? Check the gap first. 🏙️

Say the new launch is $2,400 psf and the five year old condo is $1,800. A big gap like that often pulls the older one up over time, as buyers priced out of the new project look next door. If the gap is small, say $2,400 vs $2,250, the newer one usually gives more for your money.

Most people decide this wrongly. Comment WHY to see the mistake 👇

Illustrative figures only.
